Alternative: make expanded `Metric` inherit text alignment; wrap each metric in caller-owned native elements: ```svelte
``` The feature controls `.headline-final { text-align: end }` at the desktop breakpoint and `start` below it. Shared CSS changes expanded alignment from `left` to `inherit`. No feature selector reaches component internals. This keeps responsive arrangement in the feature and adds no prop. However, inheritance becomes a public component contract: every expanded metric can change appearance under an aligned ancestor. Preserving existing behavior requires explicitly setting the shared headline container to `start` and auditing other expanded callers. Default metrics retain their existing desktop-right/mobile-left rules. Recommendation: prefer the optional typed `align?: "start" | "end"` prop for this small change. Omitted alignment preserves current behavior exactly, alignment ownership is explicit, and future callers can discover it in the component signature. The wrapper alternative has fewer API characters but introduces ambient dependencies. Document the prop and unchanged defaults in README; show an end-aligned expanded metric in the gallery. Test default preservation and explicit alignment there; test actual section-edge placement and mobile behavior in the shared headline feature on MP and funder pages.
